#### What this PR does / why we need it:

We store scheduled pods information into cache as assumedPod before binding Pod.
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/7af5a7bfc51d0455d8b2322ae9e72ed66fb1b8f9/pkg/scheduler/schedule_one.go#L741
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/7af5a7bfc51d0455d8b2322ae9e72ed66fb1b8f9/pkg/scheduler/internal/cache/cache.go#L384

And, just after binding Pod, we receive `Add` event for scheduled Pods from eventhandler and `sched.addPodToCache` will be used to add Pod to cache.
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/7af5a7bfc51d0455d8b2322ae9e72ed66fb1b8f9/pkg/scheduler/eventhandlers.go#L276

But, as described above, we've added store scheduled pods information. So, basically, scheduler doesn't update pod in cache here:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/7af5a7bfc51d0455d8b2322ae9e72ed66fb1b8f9/pkg/scheduler/internal/cache/cache.go#L503-L514

But, `Add` event contains changes not only of `.spec.NodeName` but also of `.status.Condition`. Updated here:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/edac6fce2ad4a1366a73afc8ac9ca50b2fbf7fc7/pkg/registry/core/pod/storage/storage.go#L233-L236

So, we should update cache to keep `.status.Condition` up-to-date when we receive `Add` event for scheduled Pods from eventhandler.
Otherwise, `.status.Condition` won't updated until new changes for that Pod are made.

This PR change `AddPod` method to update cached Pod any time to make sure the Pod's status is up-to-date.

issue_context.title: scheduled Pods in Kubernetes scheduler's internal cache don't have PodScheduled condition until they are next updated
issue_context.body:
### What happened?


Some Pods in Kubernetes scheduler's internal cache don't have `PodScheduled` condition in their status.

We store scheduled pods information into cache as assumedPod before binding Pod.
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/7af5a7bfc51d0455d8b2322ae9e72ed66fb1b8f9/pkg/scheduler/schedule_one.go#L741
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/7af5a7bfc51d0455d8b2322ae9e72ed66fb1b8f9/pkg/scheduler/internal/cache/cache.go#L384

And, just after binding Pod, we receive `Add` event for scheduled Pods from eventhandler and `sched.addPodToCache` will be used to add Pod to cache.
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/7af5a7bfc51d0455d8b2322ae9e72ed66fb1b8f9/pkg/scheduler/eventhandlers.go#L276

But, as described above, we've added store scheduled pods information. So, basically, scheduler doesn't update pod in cache here:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/7af5a7bfc51d0455d8b2322ae9e72ed66fb1b8f9/pkg/scheduler/internal/cache/cache.go#L503-L514

But, `Add` event contains changes not only of `.spec.NodeName` but also of `.status.Condition`. So, we should update cache to keep `.status.Condition` up-to-date when we receive `Add` event for scheduled Pods from eventhandler.
Otherwise, `.status.Condition` won't updated until new changes for that Pod are made.

### What did you expect to happen?

Kubernetes scheduler's internal cache always keeps Pod's`.status.Condition` up-to-date.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1. Create some Node.
2. Create a Pod.
3. Pod is scheduled by scheduler.
4. Check `.status.Condition` in Pods in Kubernetes scheduler's internal cache (by adding debug log or [dump](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/7af5a7bfc51d0455d8b2322ae9e72ed66fb1b8f9/pkg/scheduler/internal/cache/cache.go#L176) cache)

I think kubelet will update Pods status after they run containers, so you need to do (4) before kubelet does so. (Or doesn't use kubelet like e2e tests)

### Anything else we need to know?

/assign

Let me double-check this. (The above explanation includes my expectations, so may not be entirely correct.)

### Kubernetes version

v1.23.4

But, I guess this bug exists on latest master as well.

Does this lead to unschedulable pods or is this just for debugging purposes?

We uses `PodScheduled` condition in a custom plugin.

> Does this lead to unschedulable pods

_Mostly_ No in the real cluster. Only for a very short time (from the scheduler schedules a Pod to kubelet next updates a pod) our plugin does not behave as expected and may make some pods unschedulable.

But, when it comes to e2e testing, this bug can be troublesome.
In our e2e testing, we don't run kubelet, and no one updates Pods after the scheduler scheduled them
Then, all scheduled Pods in the scheduler cache have non-updated `PodScheduled` condition and it results in unexpected results from our plugin.

review_comments: Revisit the code, I think we should call updatePod after L506. If pod exists in `podStates` but not in `assumedPods`, we should also update the pod, right?

I don't think so. This `AddPod` func should be called only once after Pod is scheduled, and the case "pod exists in podStates but not in assumedPods" shouldn't be happened.
If that case happens, that means `AddPod` func is somehow called twice (or more) for the same Pod. And, I think we don't need to do anything in that case, and just returning an error in L528 seems enough.

>  and the case "pod exists in podStates but not in assumedPods" shouldn't be happened. 

Actually it's possible, a pod can be added without scheduler like specifying the nodeName in podSpec. But I think you're right. We'll not add the same pod twice.

> a pod can be added without scheduler like specifying the nodeName in podSpec. 

Ahh, like an unscheduled Pod is created -> a user (or a controller) specify nodeName before the scheduler schedule it -- that's a rare case, but can happen.
Let me change here as you suggest, thanks

Sorry, commented at the same time (again)

> But this matches the case !ok, no?

Ah, right. nvm, I'll remove the commit I just added.

sounds good to me.

- when `oldPod.Spec.NodeName == newPod.Spec.NodeName`, updates only PodInfo in NodeInfo. (Also, we probably need to create new methods on `framework.NodeInfo` like `UpdatePod`/`UpdatePodInfo`.)
- otherwise, deletePod -> addPod. (the current behavior.)
